newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed, front months trade higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed, front months trade higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed Wednesday, with front months moving higher in thin volume amid little market-moving news, industry sources said.
"It is a light day with not a whole lot of news, I expect we will settle pretty much unchanged (from Tuesday)," said a futures broker.

As of 1245 EST, December California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 10 cents at $23.15 after exchanging hands as high as $23.50, while January COB was trading up six cents at $20.50 after trade as high as $20.60 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds were mostly offered below Tuesday settles.
December Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 20 cents at $21.25 per MWh, while January was down 35 cents at $18.95 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds were bid at mixed levels to Tuesday's closes.
NYMEX said that as of 1225 EST, an estimated total of 56 COB and 10 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Nov 12 fell five to 3,906, while PV open interest rose 23 to 1,943, NYMEX said.
